findings.entity: PacifiCorp (subsidiary of Berkshire Hathaway Energy, which Berkshire Hathaway wholly owns)
findings.claim: US Forest Service reports found that power lines of PacifiCorp, a Berkshire Hathaway Energy subsidiary, caused the 2020 Slater fire and were the probable cause of the Archie Creek fire. In February 2026 PacifiCorp agreed to pay $575 million to settle US claims that its lines negligently started six 2020 and 2022 fires on public land; it denies liability.

findings.entity: PacifiCorp (subsidiary of Berkshire Hathaway Energy, which Berkshire Hathaway wholly owns)
findings.claim: In 2023 an Oregon jury found PacifiCorp, a Berkshire Hathaway Energy subsidiary, grossly negligent, reckless and willful over four 2020 fires; awards so far exceed $1 billion to about 200 survivors. The Court of Appeals reversed the verdict earlier in 2026, and the Oregon Supreme Court heard argument on 3 November 2026; about 2,000 further claims may depend on it.

findings.entity: HomeServices of America (subsidiary of Berkshire Hathaway Energy, which Berkshire Hathaway wholly owns)
findings.claim: In October 2023 a Missouri federal jury found HomeServices of America, a Berkshire Hathaway Energy subsidiary, and co-defendants took part in a conspiracy that had the purpose or effect of inflating home sellers’ commissions, with $1.8 billion in damages jointly. HomeServices settled in April 2024 for $250 million over four years.

A federal judge found in 2023 that BNSF, Berkshire Hathaway’s railroad, knowingly ran crude oil trains across the Swinomish reservation beyond its 1991 easement, and in 2024 ordered it to pay nearly $400 million in profits. BNSF appealed, then settled on confidential terms in November 2025; Berkshire’s annual report says BNSF apologised.

In October 2020 Berkshire agreed to pay OFAC $4.1 million over 144 apparent Iran sanctions violations by its Turkish subsidiary Iscar Turkey between 2012 and 2016. OFAC called the case egregious and found local managers hid the sales from Berkshire, which self-disclosed them.

Berkshire’s 2025 annual report lists 11,272 MW of coal plant capacity at PacifiCorp and MidAmerican (6,856 MW owned) and names coal and gas plants as BHE’s main source of greenhouse gases. BNSF had about $3.0 billion in coal freight revenue in 2025.

Berkshire reports that BHE had invested $38.0 billion in renewable generation and storage and ceased coal operations at 22 units by the end of 2025, cutting its annual greenhouse gas emissions by 30% from 2005. These are company figures, not independently verified here.

In June 2025 Buffett gave about $6 billion in Berkshire stock to five foundations, 9.4 million of about 12.4 million shares to the Gates Foundation Trust; AP put his gifts to them since 2006 at roughly $60 billion at the time of giving. In July 2026 Berkshire announced his gift of 12 million shares to four family foundations; the Gates Foundation was not among them.

ProPublica reported in 2021, from IRS records it obtained without saying how, that Buffett reported paying $23.7 million in taxes for 2014–2018 while Forbes estimated his wealth grew $24.3 billion, the lowest such rate among the 25 richest Americans. No illegality is alleged; he said he paid the taxes he owed.

ecology.reason: Berkshire’s utilities own about 6,900 MW of coal capacity and BNSF had about $3 billion in coal freight revenue in 2025. US Forest Service reports found power lines of PacifiCorp, a Berkshire Hathaway Energy subsidiary, caused or probably caused two 2020 wildfires; PacifiCorp agreed to pay $575 million to settle federal claims over six fires and denies liability. Berkshire reports a 30% cut in its energy unit’s emissions since 2005.

social.reason: Company-level problems are documented at Berkshire subsidiaries: a 2023 federal jury found HomeServices of America took part in a conspiracy that had the purpose or effect of inflating home sellers’ commissions, and a federal judge found BNSF knowingly ran oil trains across Swinomish land beyond its easement. Both later settled. No finding against him personally.

legal.reason: Company outcomes at Berkshire and its subsidiaries; no personal record found. Court findings against BNSF (trespass, nearly $400 million, settled 2025) and HomeServices (commission conspiracy, $1.8 billion jointly, settled for $250 million). PacifiCorp agreed to pay $575 million to the US over wildfires, denying liability. OFAC fined Berkshire $4.1 million in 2020 over a subsidiary’s Iran sales.

unresolved.reason: Pending at company level: the Oregon Supreme Court heard argument in November 2026 on a 2023 jury verdict against PacifiCorp, a Berkshire Hathaway Energy subsidiary, over four 2020 wildfires. The Court of Appeals reversed the verdict earlier in 2026, and about 2,000 further claims may depend on the outcome. Nothing personal found.

proposal.counterweights: Has given five foundations, including the Gates Foundation, Berkshire shares worth roughly $60 billion when given since 2006, per AP; his 2026 gift went to four family foundations only. Berkshire reports a 30% emissions cut at its energy unit since 2005.
proposal.rationale: Legal 0→2: court findings against BNSF and HomeServices (Berkshire subsidiaries) meet level 2. Unresolved 0→2: the PacifiCorp James case is pending before Oregon’s Supreme Court. Social 1→2: the same two findings are documented company-level problems; deaths in the 2020 and 2022 fires could be read under level 4, but causation and liability are contested and settled without admission. Ecology stays 3 (coal, rail, wildfires). Politics not assessed. The tax finding (f9) maps to no dimension.
